name: Inositol

lead: Inositol is a naturally occurring sugar alcohol found in fruit, beans, nuts and grains and made in the body. Supplements are used mainly for PCOS, and some looksmaxxers add it to calming or sleep stacks. Forums also discuss D-chiro-inositol raising testosterone and myo-inositol lowering androgens, even affecting jaw growth.

It forms part of cell-signaling molecules that regulate calcium and insulin signaling. Research centers on PCOS, where reported benefits include insulin sensitivity, androgen levels and cycle regularity; no trial in the sources reviewed tests it for sleep or facial development.

paras: It is taken as a powder or capsule, usually as myo-inositol or D-chiro-inositol, often in the evening as part of a calming stack. Users judge it over weeks.
Toxicity appears very low in animal data, but human side-effect information in the sources reviewed is limited. Pregnant and breastfeeding people are advised to consult a professional.

chain: Possible changes to skin or jaw growth
angle.text: Users take inositol for sleep and metabolic aims, and forums discuss D-chiro-inositol raising testosterone and myo-inositol lowering androgens, even shaping jaw growth. Trials focus on PCOS and androgen levels in women; the looksmaxxing claims have not been tested.

lead: Inositol is a sugar alcohol with the formula C6H12O6 that is a component of cell structures and acts as a signaling molecule in eukaryotic cells; myo-inositol is the most abundant form, and D-chiro-inositol is another isomer sold as a supplement [1]. It is found in fruit (oranges and cantaloupe especially), beans, nuts and grains, and is also made in the body, mainly in the kidneys [1].

Its best-studied supplement use is in polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), where Wikipedia describes reported benefits for insulin sensitivity, hyperandrogenism and cycle regularity [1]. In looksmaxxing communities it is mentioned in sleep and calming stacks, and in forum claims about hormones and jaw growth. No trial in the sources reviewed tests inositol for sleep or facial development.

paras: Inositol exists as several stereoisomers, with myo-inositol the most abundant; once called vitamin B8, it lost that classification because the body makes it [1]. It was first isolated from muscle extracts by Scherer in 1850 [1]. Inositol phosphates are central to cell signaling: inositol trisphosphate acts as a second messenger that releases intracellular calcium, work that has been cited thousands of times [2][3].

Registered trials focus on PCOS, infertility and gestational diabetes, testing myo-inositol alone, D-chiro-inositol, or a combination mixture [4][5][6][7][8]. Wikipedia describes combined myo- and D-chiro-inositol at a 40:1 ratio as commonly studied, and notes the use of high doses for trichotillomania without definitive evidence of effectiveness [1]. A registered trial in children with bipolar disorder and anxiety was withdrawn [9]. No studies were found for sleep or appearance outcomes.

Wikipedia reports very low toxicity for myo-inositol (oral rat LD50 10,000 mg/kg) but does not discuss human side effects [1]. Labels for combination products advise pregnant or breastfeeding people to ask a health professional [10].
